turns.assessment: The correlated 1–2 errored seconds and immediate protection switch-and-return across every service using och11 indicate a very brief common optical transient, not a persistent outage or client-port fault. No power, OSNR, BER, DGD, SOP-rate, amplifier, or OCM change was retained, which strongly favors a millisecond SOP transient. The only specifically exposed common location is the 78.3 km aerial segment, represented by E7 and E17 in opposite directions; the observations do not identify which directional span record should receive the repair.

proposals.rationale: E7 is the S05-to-S15 representation of the aerial segment. A fast polarization excursion can produce isolated errored seconds and momentary protection switching without a retained power, OSNR, DGD, or SOP-rate change.

E17 is the reverse-direction representation of the same-length aerial segment. It is equally consistent with the brief errors and absence of persistent optical changes, and the bidirectional line-interface errors do not resolve E7 versus E17.
A brief mechanical power excursion on the aerial span could cause the event, but unchanged OCM and receiver power make a polarization-only transient more likely.
The reverse-direction aerial span is an equivalent lower-probability location for a brief mechanical power excursion.
